test: the welcome page names the hotel, has the two-line heading and says what the board is for
what_should_happen: When the app opens on the welcome page, a small line above the heading reads "Harbour View · housekeeping". The big heading reads "Sixty rooms." with "No clipboard upstairs." on its second line, and a short paragraph under it says how every room moves through the day and what the board knows.
exact_words: Every room moves from occupied to dirty, cleaned, inspected and ready, raced against the day's arrivals.
The board knows where each one is, who is on it, and how long before its guest it was ready.

test: with every guest still in the counts read 60 rooms, 0 ready and 0 dirty
what_should_happen: On a fresh start every guest is still in their room. Once the page has read the rooms, its three counts read 60 rooms, 0 ready and 0 dirty.

reason: That the ready number is drawn in green is a colour, which a pretend browser does not paint.

test: with one room checked out the dirty count reads 1 and the other counts are unchanged
what_should_happen: Room 213's guest has checked out before the page opens. The counts come from the real hotel, so dirty reads 1 while rooms still reads 60 and ready still reads 0.

test: the picture shows rooms 209 to 215 of floor 2, each with its number and its state
what_should_happen: Beside the heading there is a small picture of a corridor. It shows exactly the seven doors 209 to 215 from floor 2, each with its number and its state word, which on a fresh start is Occupied. No other room number is in it.

test: the picture follows the hotel: a checked-out 213 shows as Dirty
what_should_happen: Room 213's guest has checked out before the page opens. The picture is drawn from the real rooms, so door 213 shows Dirty while 215 is still Occupied.

reason: Each state word drawn in its state's colour is a colour; the type shown on each door is checked on the board, where its words are given.

test: the doors are only a picture: clicking one does nothing
what_should_happen: Clicking a door in the picture, 209 or 213, does nothing. The address stays on the welcome page, the person cards are still there and no panel opens.

test: under "Who are you today?" four cards show Grace, Pradeep, Sunita and Mr Menon with their roles and blurbs
what_should_happen: Under the heading "Who are you today?" and its one-line note there are four person cards. Each card shows the person's name, their role, their one-line blurb and "Continue as" with their name.
exact_words: Each person sees their own screens. Everything they do changes the same hotel.
Runs housekeeping. Sees every room, assigns the dirty ones and inspects what others cleaned.
Checks guests out at the desk. The room turns dirty the moment he does.
Cleans the rooms she is given. Starts the clock when she begins and stops it when she is done.
Judges the morning on one number: how long before the guest each room was ready.

test: clicking 'Continue as Grace' changes the address to /supervisor/board
what_should_happen: Clicking Grace's card takes you to her first screen. The address becomes /supervisor/board.

test: clicking 'Continue as Pradeep' changes the address to /desk/checkout
what_should_happen: Clicking Pradeep's card takes you to the front desk's screen. The address becomes /desk/checkout.

test: clicking 'Continue as Sunita' changes the address to /housekeeper
what_should_happen: Clicking Sunita's card takes you to the housekeeper's screen. The address becomes /housekeeper.

test: clicking 'Continue as Mr Menon' changes the address to /manager/rooms
what_should_happen: Clicking Mr Menon's card takes you to the general manager's screen. The address becomes /manager/rooms.

test: Tab moves through the four cards in order
what_should_happen: Pressing Tab on the welcome page reaches Grace's card. Each further Tab moves to the next card: Pradeep, then Sunita, then Mr Menon.

test: Enter on a focused card opens that person's screen
what_should_happen: Tab until Sunita's card has the focus and press Enter. Her screen opens at /housekeeper, just as a click would open it.

reason: Below 1100px the cards going two per row, and below 1024px the picture moving under the heading, are layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.
At phone width the cards stacking one per row and nothing scrolling sideways are layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.
